name: reduced_character_orbit_computation

phase_0.boundary_condition: The symmetric group acting on a finite set of points.

VINIT.justification: The state before any group action or set definition occurs.

TANCH.justification: The complete classification of all points under the group action.

AFWD.justification: The mapping of a point to its image under a group element.

AREV.justification: The mapping of a point back to its preimage using the group inverse.

CLINK.justification: The sequential application of two group elements to form a single transformation.

IMSCRIB.justification: The group element that maps every point to itself.

FSPLIT.justification: The branching of a point into either a known orbit or a new candidate orbit.

FFUSE.justification: The recombination of tested points into a single verified orbit structure.

EVALT.justification: The confirmation that a point belongs to the current orbit under computation.

EVALF.justification: The confirmation that a point does not belong to the current orbit.

ENGAGR.justification: A state where a point appears to belong to two orbits before the relation is resolved.

IFIX.justification: The permanent storage of a canonical representative for a computed orbit.

phase_2.split_input: A candidate point and a group action
phase_2.fuse_result: The original set of points partitioned by the group action

phase_3.void_description: No points or group elements defined
phase_3.true_description: Point is reachable under the group action
phase_3.false_description: Point is unreachable under the group action
phase_3.both_description: Point is undergoing a transitive reduction check

steps.domain_action: Initialize the set of points and the generating set of the group
Identify the identity element of the group action
Record the first point as the initial orbit representative
Test the next point against the current orbit representative
Apply the group generator to the representative
Confirm the image point belongs to the current orbit
Rejoin the confirmed point to the orbit structure
Compose the generator with the next group element
Test if the new image point is already recorded
Apply the inverse generator to verify the path
Identify a point that cannot be reached from the current representative
Rejoin the non-member point to the set of unvisited points
Record the non-member as a new orbit representative
Hold a point that is reachable via two different generator paths
Resolve the transitive relation between the paths
Commit the final orbit partition to memory
Close the computation once all points are assigned to orbits

phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Pointer passing between orbit data structures
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: A breadth-first search queue for point traversal
phase_5.alfs_store: The Cayley table of the acting group

phase_6.cycle_cost: Computational cycles per group action application
phase_6.post_cycle_state: A set of points partitioned into disjoint orbits
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The information content of the set is preserved through a bijective mapping.
